Entry 0 of m_streams (this+0x14) is the position stream: IBuffer::map 0x5a1adc (the CONST read map, access 0) is called at 0x5a0ee0, the first element is base + entry.offset + entry.field0e * first (0x5a0ee8..0x5a0efc), and the box comes from glitch::core::computeBoundingBox 0x6a48cc with value type field0a, component count field0c, stride field0e and count last - first (0x5a0f00..0x5a0f14). The mapping is released through the SMapBuffer release 0x5a0e28 before the quantized branch (0x5a0f1c..0x5a0f28). With bit 2 of m_flags set (now named kFlagQuantized 0x0004) both corners become box * m_quantization[0] + m_quantization[1], component by component (0x5a0f2c..0x5a0fd8). Deviations, all named: the map and release are written out instead of through SVertexStream::SMapBuffer::reset because that reset's int32_t access parameter cannot select the const read map (E_BUFFER_MAP_ACCESS and E_BUFFER_READ_MAP_ACCESS are both int32_t aliases, so overload resolution on a non-const buffer picks 0x5a19f0 instead); the release is guarded on the mapped base, the port's SMapBuffer convention (the original tests base + offset); the quantized branch also tests m_quantization.size() >= 2 because the port keeps the trailing block in a std::vector. The dependency glitch::core::computeBoundingBox 0x6a48cc had NO definition in the tree (its note had been right, not stale) and was written in the same pass: glitch-core-io/include/glitch-core-io/core/bounding_box.hpp. THE `m_quantization.size() >= 2` GUARD: SETTLED by glitch-video/tests/vertex_streams_quantization_guard_test.cpp, which was written for it. It is NOT reachable from any table this class's constructors produce: the constructor lays out 2 * (count0c + 1) records (checked for count0c = 0, 1 and 7, through both 0x5a113c and the 7-argument allocate 0x5a1270), clone() 0x5a1310 rebuilds the same count from count0c, and no method shrinks it - so the guard's condition is always true for a normally constructed table, and the test shows the dequantized box for one. It IS reachable, and load-bearing, through port-only state: m_quantization and m_flags are public, so clearing the vector (or using the port-only default constructor and setting the flag) makes the guard the only thing between the call and an out-of-bounds read. The test does exactly that and asserts the box stays unquantized; deleting the size test from the body makes the test fault (measured). Verdict: legitimate defensive guard, not dead code to remove - it never changes reconstructed behaviour, and removing it would turn a defined no-op into UB.

THE FIELD DECISION: entry +0x00 is the SData* itself, not a 4-byte word that needs a reinterpretation. Three independent proofs: (1) get returns a record whose +4 is the text, and the listing compares the entry word + 4 against it, so the word is the record start, i.e. the pointer; (2) the renderer constructor 0x5d3124 stores each SShaderParameterDef into an entry and takes a use on its +0x00 (loc_5D35F0: `LDR R1,[R2]; if (R1) ++*(int*)R1`), the SSharedString handle pattern, and SSharedString::operator= (0x5daf94) puts exactly the pointer get returns into such a word; (3) IShader::getParameterID(char const*,stage,index) 0x5e4b74 runs the identical compare over the identical 16-byte record. So the port's uint8_t unknown00[4] was the wrong model; it is now `const void* name`, the same modelling STechnique::name (material_renderer.hpp:71) already uses, and SParameterEntry is accordingly no longer pinned to 16 bytes on this host (material_parameters_part_1b.hpp now asserts field ORDER, not size). BLOCKED only on pixel_format::convert's completeness: the two converts it issues go through the port's subset model (row 0x5f95ac is skipped), so a format pair that model refuses leaves the destination as it was.

Re-verified against the listing (chunk_032.c:35950-35969) and the body at image.cpp is the listing's: with a non-null target it compares the target's +0x10/+0x14 with this image's and, when both match, builds the zero position and calls copyTo(target, position, flags) at 0x60090c, otherwise copyToScaling(target->m_data, target->m_width, target->m_height, target->m_format, target->m_pitch, flags) at 0x600fcc, so the target is the DESTINATION and this image is the source. RECONSTRUCTED now: the one item that held it back - the equal-size path reaching the mirrored 0x600708, which wrote this image instead of the target - is fixed (row 0x600708), and the wrapper itself (0x60090c) is the listing's. The remaining limit is the port's convert being a subset model (row 0x5f95ac), which is that row's gap, not this one's: the same slice of convert sits behind every CImage transfer row, and 0x600fcc is reconstructed with the same dependency. A format pair convert does not model returns 0 and writes nothing, which is convert's named limit.
Verified 0x601800 by disassembling: it is one instruction, B 0x60177c, so CImage::copyToScalingBoxFilter is literally CImage::copyToScaling. Reproduced as a forward in image.cpp; it has no other gap.

Hex-Rays 0x601804 matched. The teardown is guarded by m_ownsData (+0x29): the pixel block is freed first, then, when m_hasMipmaps (+0x28) is set and the level array exists, every level is freed until a null slot and the array itself last, with each level pointer nulled as it is freed. Deviation, deliberate: the original walks the array with an unbounded do/while that only terminates because the chain is fully initialised when built; this port also stops at m_mipLevels so a partially built chain cannot run the walk off the end. NOTE, left in the tree deliberately and re-worded after the constructor pass, with the reachable cases named: the m_ownsData guard covers the level ARRAY as well as the block (LDRB at 0x601810, then BNE 0x6018a8 skips the array) and it has to stay, because on the adopt path of 0x6021f8 the array is the caller's and freeing it unconditionally would free memory the image never allocated. The price, now that the data-taking constructors are in: 0x6027e8 with the second bool clear and a non-zero level count leaks the void*[levels + 1] array that constructor made for itself (and its block as well when its first bool was clear too), and 0x6021f8's copy path with the second bool clear leaks the block and the chain initData made. Nothing in the object records who allocated the array, so closing this would mean inventing a member the original does not have, so the leak is kept and named here. Neither case is reached by a caller the original has: 0x6021f8 has no call sites at all, and the 0x6027e8 call sites the port can see pass own set (JPG 0x604e6c uses the 5-argument form with own set, DDS 0x60486c and ATC 0x603204 both pass adopt set / own set). Verified by checks in glitch-video/tests/image_fill_test (registered with ctest, passing), which build owning images of 4x4 and 8x8 and let them go out of scope.
The base-object destructor; the original's body at 0x6018b8 is the same teardown as D1 at 0x601804, so one C++ destructor definition emits both symbols.
The deleting destructor, emitted by the compiler from the same C++ destructor; not written separately.

Hex-Rays 0x601988 matched. Pitch is pixel_format::computePitch(m_format, m_width) (the two words it passes are +0x20 and +0x10); when m_dataSize is 0 it becomes pitch * m_height; the data block is allocated only when m_data is null, which is what lets a caller install its own buffer first. The mip chain runs only for the allocate flag with m_hasMipmaps set and m_mipData still null: the level count is the halvings of (width,height) down to 1 (the original special-cases 1x1 to 4 bytes), the level array is new void*[levels+1] and is terminated by a null entry, and each level is height * PFDTable[format].bytesPerBlock (+0x15) * width bytes. Deviation: the original zeroes each level with a byte that advances by 15 per level (v18 += 15); that fill byte is cosmetic, so this port use memset 0. Compiles (check_tu.sh OK).

Body verified against the 0x601b10 listing (chunk_032.c:36189-36227) and the row's single missing item is now present: with a non-null source the source's format, the requested size and the source's mip flag are taken over, initData(true) allocates the block (and a chain when the source has one), and pixel_format::convert is called with source pointer = source->m_data + position.Y * source->m_pitch + position.X * PFDTable[m_format].bytesPerBlock (+0x15), srcPitch = source->m_pitch, BOTH formats = m_format (the source's own), dstPitch = m_pitch, width/height = the requested size, flip 0, and the result ignored. That call takes convert's srcFormat == dstFormat copy() branch (0x5ee40c), which is now reconstructed (row 0x5ee40c): rows = height, pitch = computePitch(12, 2) = 8, and the source pitch (16) differs, so it is one memcpy per row, the source advancing by its own pitch. Measured in glitch-video/tests/image_fill_test.cpp: a 4x4 format-12 source whose bytes are their own offsets gives a 2x2 sub-image at (1,1) with row 0 = bytes 20..27 and row 1 = bytes 36..43, which is the source pointer offset 1*16 + 1*4 = 20 and then + the source pitch. Deviation: the null-source guard (the listing dereferences). The PARTIAL comment above image.cpp:761 is now stale and should be dropped by the file's owner. check_tu.sh OK.

The C2 form: the disassembly at 0x601c24 is the same body as the C1 at 0x601b10 (same instruction sequence), so one C++ definition emits both symbols. Its single missing item is gone: convert's srcFormat == dstFormat copy() branch (0x5ee40c) is reconstructed, so the sub-image's pixels are transferred; see the 0x601b10 row for the measured transfer.

Body written from the 0x601d38 listing: the requested format goes to +0x20 first, the refcount is stored 0, data/level array/pitch/dataSize/level count clear, m_hasMipmaps 0 and m_ownsData 1; with a source image the source's width, height and mip flag are taken over, initData(true) allocates (and builds a level chain when the source has one), then pixel_format::convert(source->m_format, source->m_data, source->m_pitch, m_format, m_data, m_pitch, m_width, m_height, false) runs over the whole image. On a 0 result the failure path at 0x601dfc stores format 39, frees and clears the pixel block, frees the chain level by level until a null slot and then the array, and leaves dataSize 0, ownsData 0, height 0 and width 0; the original does NOT clear +0x0c there (the destructor then skips it because ownsData is 0) and leaves m_mipLevels and m_hasMipmaps as they were, and the port keeps both details. Which format pairs succeed is convert's coverage (row 0x5f95ac), not this body's. Verified in glitch-video/tests/image_fill_test: RGB565 -> ARGB4444 is compared byte for byte against a direct convert call with the same arguments (format order, pitches and dimensions), and a compressed-destination pair both trees refuse takes the failure path with format 39, a null block and ownsData 0, with a mip-carrying source so the level free runs. check_tu.sh OK.
The C2 form: 0x601eb0 is the same body as the C1 at 0x601d38 (92 instructions, 368 bytes), so one C++ definition emits both symbols. See the 0x601d38 row.

Hex-Rays 0x602028 matched: size -> +0x10/+0x14, format -> +0x20, m_hasMipmaps (+0x28) takes the argument, m_ownsData (+0x29) is 1, and initData allocates. The reference count is stored as 0, not left at IReferenceCounted's default of 1, which is what every original constructor does. Verified by checks in glitch-video/tests/image_fill_test (registered with ctest, passing): 4x4 format 12 gives pitch 16, dataSize 64, an allocated block, no mip chain, and fill writes 0x563412FF into it; 4x4 format 5 with the mip flag gives pitch 8, dataSize 32 and a built, null-terminated level array. Known gap, not in this row: ~CImage is still not reconstructed, so an image built here owns memory nothing releases yet.
Compiler-emitted alias of the C1 definition at 0x602028 (the original's C1 and C2 bodies are identical); one C++ definition emits both symbols, so nothing separate is written.

Hex-Rays 0x602110 matched: as the hasMipmaps form with the flag clear, so initData allocates the block but builds no mip chain. Same reference-count note (stored 0). Verified by the checks in glitch-video/tests/image_fill_test.
Compiler-emitted alias of the C1 definition at 0x602110; one C++ definition emits both symbols.

Body written from the 0x6021f8 listing. The FIRST bool is the one tested (0x60226c) and the SECOND goes to m_ownsData (+0x29). First bool set adopts the caller's block and level array: +0x08/+0x0c are set to 0x0badf00d so initData (which allocates only when the data pointer is null) allocates nothing, then both caller pointers are stored, the count restarts at 0 and the caller's array is walked (0x6023d0-0x602400) to recover the level count, with m_hasMipmaps set only when the walk reaches a null entry at width and height 1. First bool clear copies: with mip data the flag is set BEFORE initData, so initData allocates the block and a full chain, level 0 is copied with the pitch * height count and each caller level into the slot initData made for it with size (height * bitsPerPixel(+0x16) * width) >> 3 over the halved dimensions; with no mip data only the block is allocated and filled. Two listing details are NOT reproduced, both unreachable and named in the source comment: the cleanup at 0x60234c is dead (it is entered only from 0x602338, by which point this path cleared m_mipLevels to 0 at 0x6022ac while the copy count is at least 1, so the BLS at 0x602348 always returns; its own loop at 0x60236c branches back to the same free unconditionally and would spin), and the two loops have no bound of their own, so a caller chain shorter than the image's chain reads the next slot and memcpys from it - the port keeps that shape. The constructor has no call sites (its only cross-reference is 0x7e258). Verified in glitch-video/tests/image_fill_test, which exercises all four paths: adopt with and without a level array, and copy with and without mip data (16- and 4-byte levels land in the chain). check_tu.sh OK.

The C2 form: its disassembly at 0x602434 is the same body as the C1 at 0x6021f8 (same instruction sequence, and one C++ definition emits both symbols), so nothing separate is written. See the 0x6021f8 row.

Body rewritten from the 0x602670 listing, which corrects this row's earlier note. The branch at 0x6026d8 tests the FIRST bool (LDRB R6,[SP,#arg_0]; CMP R6,#0; BNE 0x602704), not m_ownsData, and the two paths are the opposite way round from what the old note claimed: first bool SET stores 0x0badf00d into +0x08 (0x60270c) so initData - whose allocation test is 'only when the data pointer is null' - leaves the buffer alone, then stores the caller's pointer over it (0x602718); first bool CLEAR lets initData allocate and memcpys pitch * height bytes of the caller's block in (0x6026f8). The SECOND bool goes to m_ownsData (+0x29) and only decides who frees the block. So the first flag means 'adopt the caller's block'. The earlier port branched on own and reproduced neither path; that deviation is gone, and the three call sites confirm the reading: the JPG loader 0x604e6c and the DDS loader 0x60486c both pass adopt 1 with own 1 for buffers they allocated for the load, and glitch-scene-collada-gui CGUITTFont passes (false, true) for a temporary it keeps. m_mipData stays null in this form. The port keeps its null guard on the memcpy where the original dereferences the argument. Verified in glitch-video/tests/image_fill_test: adopt 1/own 0 makes m_data the caller's buffer (fill then writes into it) and the copy path allocates its own block and copies the caller's bytes. check_tu.sh OK.
The C2 form: 0x60272c is the same body as the C1 at 0x602670, so one C++ definition emits both symbols. See the 0x602670 row for the flag semantics, which the earlier note had inverted.

Body written from the 0x6027e8 listing, and the two unsigned arguments are now named for what the listing stores: the fourth after the data pointer goes to +0x1c (the data size) and the fifth to +0x24 (the number of mip levels below level 0), not a pitch and a size as the header comment used to say - the DDS loader 0x60486c passes computeSizeInBytes(...) and the header's mipmapCount - 1 there, and the ATC 0x603204 and PVR 0x6060f4 loaders do the same. m_ownsData takes the second bool, m_hasMipmaps is cleared and +0x18 is not stored (initData computes it). First bool set adopts the caller's single buffer via the 0x0badf00d store at 0x602868; first bool clear lets initData allocate dataSize bytes and memcpys exactly that many. With a non-zero level count the constructor then allocates its own void*[levels + 1] (0x6028b4) and fills it with pointers into that buffer, the entry for level i + 1 being the buffer plus the sum of computeMipmapSizeInBytes(format, width, height, 0 .. i), null-terminated (0x6028e8-0x602928). m_hasMipmaps stays clear on purpose: the levels live inside m_data, so the destructor frees the block once and the array once and never the levels individually. Verified in glitch-video/tests/image_fill_test: a 4x4 format 12 buffer with a supplied size of 64 and two levels gives the array 64 and 80 bytes into m_data and a null terminator, the same with the first bool clear lands in the image's own copy of the buffer, and a zero level count leaves the array null. check_tu.sh OK.
The C2 form: 0x602938 is the same body as the C1 at 0x6027e8 (same instruction sequence), so one C++ definition emits both symbols. See the 0x6027e8 row.
